messages:
dmitri: Quick sync: after yesterday's canary we observed a race where two nodes briefly claimed residency for the same prefix during a demote->prefetch->revoke pattern. Caused duplicated KV fetches and memory blips.
anya: Oof. Was this from the new soft-demote path or the older handoff code?
dmitri: Soft-demote interacting with an immediate aggressive prefetch on the target. Timeline: origin marks demote, target receives hint and starts prefetch, origin gets a lease_revoke and clears residency. Network reordering made both persist local residency around the same time.
liam: Do we have the RPC traces? curious whether the ack ordering is reversed or if persistence lag is the culprit.
dmitri: Attached trace snippet: `RPC@t1: handoff_request->target`, `persist_local_residency@t2: target`, `origin_clear@t3`, but origin_clear arrived before target persisted in some runs.
sophie: Long term we need a linearized ownership transfer. Short term, can we add a simple guard: require origin to see a persisted marker on metadata store before clearing?
dmitri: That's one of the options discussed. Concern: extra round-trip on hot handoffs could regress tail latency.
liam: Could we optimize by writing a tiny metadata key (prefix:handoff_pending) in the fast consensus store only for contested prefixes? Most handoffs uncontested -> skip. Contested -> pay cost.
anya: How do we detect contested preemptively? Maybe track concurrent prefetch attempts count per-prefix in-memory and switch to the safe path when >1.
sophie: Good idea. Also add a TTL on the pending marker so we don't leak state. 20s default? configurable.
dmitri: I sketched a hybrid proto: 1) Origin writes pending(epoch) to metadata. 2) Target fetches, persists residency with epoch and responds. 3) Origin reads confirmed epoch and then CAS-clears its residency. 4) If something times out, mark zombie and schedule repair.
liam: For the CAS step, use metadata store's compare-and-swap on the owner key so we have one authoritative source of truth. That prevents two persisting owners.
anya: If both nodes persist local residency before CAS, clients might still see duplicate reads for a short window. Can we provide read-level fencing? return prefix_version with KV responses, and require clients to accept only increasing versions.
sophie: For internal correctness, add `conflict_detected` metric and auto-evict duplicate owners if metadata disagrees. Also implement a small reconcile worker that watches `pending` keys and reconciles ownership every 30s.
dmitri: We'll need tests: a chaos harness that delays RPCs, reorders messages, and forces simultaneous demote/prefetch on the same prefix. Add to CI and run on canary.
liam: I can add the harness. Pseudocode: ```bash
# start two nodes A/B
# create prefix owned by A
# concurrently: A.demote(); B.start_prefetch(); inject network delay A.final_clear
# assert: metadata ends up with single owner, duplicates <= 1
```
anya: Also test heavy churn scenarios to measure memory amplification and duplicate fetch counts. We should track delta in network egress too.
sophie: Dashboard items: histogram of handoff latency (fast vs metadata path), counter for pending TTL expirations, gauge of in-flight handoffs.
dmitri: Ownership: Liam owns the chaos test + CI; Anya and Sophie will spec metrics and dashboards; I'll own the RFC update and rollout checklist. Infra: please approve canary.
ci-bot: Canary rollout scheduled -> `handoff-metadata-bridge` -> redwood-canary-5 -> staged 5/25/60. Link: https://deploys/internal/handoff-metadata-bridge
liam: One implementation detail: the metadata writes must be idempotent and include epoch + origin-id so retries are safe. Also support a backoff before origin final-clear to reduce edge collisions.
anya: Backoff is cheap but not sufficient. The metadata CAS is the strong correctness signal; backoff just reduces contention probability.
sophie: Add a migration note: metadata schema version bump and migration script. Include TTL defaults and a feature flag to flip the safe path on.
dmitri: Agreed. Contracts to document in RFC follow-up: 1) single authoritative owner in metadata store, 2) prefix_version monotonicity for clients, 3) eventual repair for zombie owners, 4) opt-in fast-path for low contention.
liam: I'll open PR for test harness and add chaos job.
anya: I'll draft the dashboard panels.
sophie: I'll write the rollout playbook and failure recovery steps.
dmitri: Thanks everyone. I'll post canary results here once infra approves. :rocket:
